uncertain.text: mauuais, ou infaiſable {b}. & faluſt-il eſpandre, ren-
uncertain.note: the word-break sign between 'faluſt' and 'il' is a single small dot set at mid x-height (body-1.jpg, 8x), clearly higher than the baseline dots used for periods on this page (cf. 'les parens.' on line 3, same strip). Read as an intra-line hyphen ('faluſt-il', the usual inversion), but it is a round dot, not the slanted double stroke used at line ends, so it could be read as a period ('faluſt. il'). Reconciler should decide.

uncertain.text: uerſer & perdre le ſang de la moitié des hommes, voire
uncertain.note: printed with no gap, 'deshommes' (body-1.jpg, 6x); normalized to two words per §1. 'des hommes,voire' likewise printed tight after the comma.

uncertain.text: Sichæus ſon couſin germain & mari de Dido ſa ſeut,
uncertain.note: sic: the last letter of 'ſeut' is a t (crossbar and curved foot visible at 7x, body-2.jpg), not an r; the sense wants 'ſeur' (sœur). Transcribed as printed.

uncertain.text: manifeſter Amphiaraus ſon mari, qu's'eſtoit caché pour
uncertain.note: sic: printed 'qu' + apostrophe + round s + apostrophe + 'eſtoit' (body-3.jpg, 7x); sense wants 'qui ſ'eſtoit'. Transcribed as printed.

uncertain.text: n'aller poinr a la guerre de Thebes, de peur d'eſtre tué
uncertain.note: sic: 'poinr' — the final letter is an r (no crossbar, r-arm at 7x), not a t. Also 'Thebes ,de' is printed with a space before the comma, normalized per §1.

uncertain.text: quel aiguillon de recouurer le riche ioyau qu'Adraſtus
uncertain.note: the compositor leaves a visible gap after the apostrophe ('qu' Adraſtus'); closed up, as in every finished page of this edition. Same at blocks[0].lines[14] ('d' eſtre').

uncertain.text: comme luy auoit eſté predit {e}. Sur quoy le Pœte s'ecri-
uncertain.note: the raised italic 'e' after 'predit' is read as the marker for margin note e (Cicero, sixth Verrine / Aeneid VI, which is the Amphiaraus-Eriphyle reference), not as the final letter of 'predite'. Without it the page would have a note e with no marker.

uncertain.text: reux & excellent en toute vertuſ, ne reformida rien en
uncertain.note: the letter after 'vertu' is a full-height long ſ (left nub at x-height, ascender, slight descender) in both places where the word occurs (body-4.jpg and body-5.jpg at 9x): word-final long s, which is unusual. Transcribed 'vertuſ'; a reader could write 'vertus'. Same at blocks[2].lines[6].

uncertain.text: en quelque lieu Saluſte, renuerſe la foy, la probité &
uncertain.note: a small extra dot sits on the baseline between 'Saluſte' and the comma (body-5.jpg, 7x) — a broken sort or ink speck; not transcribed. The print also sets a space before the comma, normalized per §1.
'Martin' is set with a wide justification gap ('Mart in') at the end of the line; transcribed as one word per §1.

uncertain.text: nee ladite de ROLS à le pourſuyure.
uncertain.note: small capitals: full-height R followed by small-capital O L S (as on page 44); transcribed as ordinary capitals per §3.

no period after ANNOT: checked at 12x (body-7.jpg), the space between T and X is clean. Other annotation heads in this edition print 'ANNOT.' / 'ANNOTAT.', so this may be a compositor's omission; transcribed as printed.

the 'c.' at the end of the third line is taken as part of note b's text (a second citation, 'c. panor. en la xxxvij. diſtinction'), not as the key of a separate note: the note actually keyed c ('Vergile au j. des Aeneides.') is printed lower, exactly beside the body line that carries marker {c}, whereas this 'c.' stands six body lines above it. If the reconciler prefers, note b would be lines 1-3 and a note c would be 'panor. en la x- / xxvij. diſtin- / ction.'

the numeral ends in the ij/ÿ form (i with two dots and a j descender); transcribed 'ij' per §2. Same in margin_notes[2].lines[2] ('iij.'), margin_notes[4].lines[1] ('iij.') and margin_notes[7].lines[3] ('ij.'). With the 'x-' at the end of the previous line the number is xxxvij.

the key glyph is a small blotted letter, c or e at the margin's native resolution (margin-1.jpg, 9x is the limit). Read as 'c' because the marker sequence on the page is b c d e f g h i, because this note stands exactly beside the body line carrying {c}, and because Aeneid I is the Pygmalion/Sichæus reference. The next note's key (before 'Ciceron en la ſixieſme Verrine') is unambiguously 'e'.
the final punctuation is faint and broken (margin-2.jpg, 15x): it reads as a small slanted wedge, i.e. a comma, but a worn period cannot be excluded.
capital I and lowercase l are not distinguishable in this italic; read 'Iude' (for Justinian's Novel 'Vt iudices sine quoquo suffragio', Coll. ij), but 'lude' is what the shape alone gives.

printed 'auxParalelles.' with no gap; normalized per §1. Same normalization in margin_notes[0].lines[3] ('panor.en la'), margin_notes[5].lines[1] ('enla vie'), margin_notes[6].lines[1] ('moth.c.ix,') and margin_notes[7].lines[0] ('Parag.j.ſur').
